results.name: Long natural broadband complaint (about 400 words)
results.query: Hello, I am writing because this has been going on for far too long and I would like someone to look at it properly. About three weeks ago we moved house and the provider connected the fibre on the same day. At first everything was fine. Then on the second Sunday the internet started dropping in the evening, usually between eight and eleven, for a few minutes at a time. My husband works from home and I study online, so we both notice straight away. We restarted the router several times, and once we left it unplugged overnight. We moved the router away from the microwave and the cordless handset, and we replaced the power adapter with the spare one from the box. Nothing changed. I called the helpline twice and both times I was asked to restart the router, which we had already done. A technician visited last Thursday and said the line looked fine, but the problem came back the same night. I have checked the cable at the wall and it is firmly seated. The lights on the box are steady green when everything works. When the internet drops, the internet light blinks for a while and then returns. Our neighbour on the first floor says his connection is fine, so I do not think it is the whole building. Last night it dropped four times between nine and ten, and each time it came back by itself after about two or three minutes. During one of those drops I plugged my laptop into the router with the yellow cable that came in the box, and it lost the connection at the same moment as the wireless devices. I did not change any settings on the router and I have not installed anything new in the house except a second television. We pay for the three hundred megabit plan, and when it works the speed is close to that, so it is not a slow speed problem. I would like to know what else can be tried, and whether the line can be examined again, because we are paying for a service that we cannot rely on in the evenings. Please do not simply ask me to restart the router again, because that has already been done many times. Thank you for your help.
expected: Recognise one intermittent-broadband issue, not several.
Keep the previous restarts, router move, adapter swap, cable check and technician visit as attempted.
Recognise that the wired laptop also dropped, and do not ask the wired-versus-wireless question again.
Do not repeat the router restart; do not claim a confirmed fault.

historical_cases.resolution:
Ticket syn_ticket_ID01_02; AI-authored synthetic; outcome: simulated_resolved.
Simulated finding: optical loss events align with rain and a technician finds moisture at an external joint
Step 1: Record the start and end of each interruption and whether it coincides with wet weather.
Step 2: Ask whether a wired device also loses internet during the same interruption; record the fibre-box light labels.
Step 3: Ask line support to compare optical-loss logs with the reported interruption times. If line loss is present, request a technician to inspect external joints for moisture.
Step 4: Only if support confirms that optical loss events align with rain and a technician finds moisture at an external joint: have an authorised technician repair and seal the confirmed damaged joint.
Step 5: After the authorised remedy, verify that line monitoring shows no optical-loss events during a later wet-weather check and the customer reports no repeat drop.

historical_cases.title: Intermittent broadband support case
historical_cases.resolution:
Ticket syn_ticket_ID02_02; AI-authored synthetic; outcome: simulated_resolved.
Simulated finding: the line stays synchronized and provider monitoring shows peak-hour congestion on the access segment
Step 1: Record when the evening drops start, how long they last, and whether the connection drops or only slows.
Step 2: Ask whether a wired device also loses internet during the evening problem; do not repeat a completed wired test.
Step 3: Ask network support whether the line stays connected during the evening problem and whether monitoring shows congestion on the local access segment.
Step 4: Only if support confirms that the line stays synchronized and provider monitoring shows peak-hour congestion on the access segment: ask network operations to rebalance the affected capacity and monitor the next busy period.
Step 5: After the authorised remedy, verify that the next evening wired check shows no repeat packet loss or dropped calls.
Simulated completion: the next evening wired check shows no repeat packet loss or dropped calls
